title: The Serial Validator
briefing: Counterfeit motherboards are sneaking into our supply chain! Real ByteWorks serials look exactly like MB-2041-AX: MB, a dash, 4 digits, a dash, then 2 capital letters. The fakes are close but never quite right. Build a pattern-matcher that spots them all.
hints: \d means a digit, [A-Z] means a capital letter and {4} means 'exactly 4 of the thing before'. ^ means the start and $ means the end, so without them 'XMB-2041-AX' would sneak through!

re.match(pattern, text) gives a match (truthy) or None. Use it inside a list comprehension's if. re.findall(r"\d{4}", text) returns every 4-digit number. re.sub(pattern, replacement, text) swaps matches out.

pattern = r"^MB-\d{4}-[A-Z]{2}$" / genuine = [s for s in scans if re.match(pattern, s)] / counterfeit = [s for s in scans if not re.match(pattern, s)] / batch_numbers = re.findall(r"\d{4}", memo) / redacted = re.sub(r"\d", "#", phone)
bonus: Write a pattern that matches UK-style postcodes like EH1 1AB, or email addresses. Test it with re.fullmatch.
